KEY MESSAGE 1...Unsettled conditions continue for much of the area 
today...before transitioning to more limited areas of upslope/lake 
effect showers tonight through Saturday night.

As we push through today and tonight...the broad surface low over 
northeast Ohio/northwestern PA will gradually consolidate and lift 
northeast across our latitude this morning...before sliding down the 
Saint Lawrence Valley and across northern New England this afternoon 
and tonight. At the same time...its parent closed low will trail a 
bit behind...with this latter feature crossing our area this 
afternoon before moving on to Maine tonight. The deep...moist...and 
gradually cooling cyclonic flow around the surface and upper lows 
will lead to additional occasional showers today...with the greatest 
coverage of these found across western New York. With 850 mb temps 
also falling back to -2C to -3C with the passage of the upper 
low...some areas of lake enhancement will also likely develop east 
of Lake Erie this afternoon as winds turn more westerly. While the 
majority of today's showers will be in the form of plain 
rain...cooling thermal profiles may allow for some wet snow to mix 
across the higher terrain of the southern Tier as we push through 
the day...thought with very marginal sfc temps in place these will 
should produce little if any accumulation. 

Tonight and Saturday a general westerly cyclonic flow in the wake of 
the departing system will tend to focus some limited/modest upslope 
and lake effect rain showers east of the lakes...with these getting 
a brief temporary boost later tonight and Saturday as a trailing 
swath of deeper wraparound moisture/DCVA slides across the area from 
west to east. Following the passage of this latter feature...drying 
out of the column and gradually warming temps aloft should support 
only some limited lake effect showers east and east-northeast of the 
lakes as our flow backs to west-southwesterly Saturday night. 
Throughout the tonight-Saturday period thermal profiles again look 
to be mild enough to support mainly rain...with some just wet snow 
mixing in across the higher terrain at times and unlikely to produce 
much if any accumulation. Outside of the areas of upslope and lake 
effect precipitation...any showers should be much more scattered 
tonight through Saturday.

2) A brief period of mainly dry weather Sunday...before more 
widespread showers return later Sunday and Sunday night. 

On Sunday a low-amplitude ridge will cross our area during the 
morning...with this and continued warming of the column bringing an 
end to any leftover lake effect showers across the North Country... 
while otherwise providing us with a brief interlude of dry weather 
that should last through most of the day. The next mid-level trough 
and its attendant surface low will then eject northeastward from the 
Tennessee and central Mississippi valleys and across our area late 
Sunday through Sunday night...with deepening moisture and attendant 
height falls/DCVA aloft providing us with another round of 
widespread rain showers.

3) A few more lake effect rain and snow showers southeast of the 
lakes Monday/Monday night...then mainly dry Tuesday through 
Thursday. 

The next mid-level trough and surface low will quickly exit off to 
our northeast Monday morning...with a westerly to west-northwesterly 
flow of colder air in its wake leading to another round of upslope 
and lake effect rain and snow showers east and east-southeast of 
both lakes. While this colder airmass will feature 850 mb temps 
falling to between -6C and -9C and will therefore be supportive of 
more of a general rain/snow mix...moisture looks to become pretty 
limited in short order during Monday...with this and marginal 
surface temps both helping to greatly limit the organization of the 
showers and any potential accumulations. Building ridging and 
increasing drying/subsidence will then bring any leftover lake 
effect to an end during Tuesday...with dry/quiet weather then 
ensuing through at least Thursday as the ridge settles to...then 
lingers along the Carolina coastline.
